learningObjectives.title: The Cold War: superpower tensions and rivalries

questions.q: The Cold War was a prolonged rivalry primarily between:
questions.explain: The Cold War pitted the capitalist USA against the communist USSR and their blocs.

questions.q: The Truman Doctrine (1947) committed the USA to:
questions.explain: The Truman Doctrine pledged support to nations resisting communism (containment).

questions.q: The Berlin Blockade (1948-49) was overcome by the Western powers through the:
questions.explain: The Berlin Airlift supplied West Berlin by air until the Soviets lifted the blockade.

questions.q: The Western military alliance formed in 1949 was:
questions.explain: NATO (1949) was the Western alliance; the Warsaw Pact (1955) was the Soviet bloc's response.

questions.q: The Cuban Missile Crisis (1962) was:
options: A nuclear standoff over Soviet missiles in Cuba
A civil war in Cuba only
questions.explain: The crisis brought the superpowers close to nuclear war before a negotiated withdrawal.

questions.q: 'Containment' was the policy of:
questions.explain: Containment sought to limit Soviet and communist expansion.

questions.q: Detente in the 1970s refers to:
options: An easing of Cold War tensions
questions.explain: Detente marked reduced tensions and arms-control agreements between the superpowers.

questions.q: The Berlin Wall fell in:
questions.explain: The fall of the Berlin Wall in 1989 symbolised the collapse of communist control in Eastern Europe.

questions.q: The Soviet Union was formally dissolved in:
questions.explain: The USSR dissolved in 1991, ending the Cold War.

questions.q: The Korean War (1950-53) is best described as a Cold War:
questions.explain: Korea became a proxy war between communist and Western-backed forces.

questions.q: Stalin was the authoritarian leader of:
questions.explain: Stalin led the Soviet Union; Hitler led Germany, Mussolini Italy, Mao China.

questions.q: The Second World War in Europe began with Germany's 1939 invasion of:
questions.explain: The invasion of Poland triggered declarations of war by Britain and France.

questions.q: India achieved independence from Britain in:
questions.explain: Indian independence in 1947 was a landmark in 20th-century decolonisation.

questions.q: The nuclear arms race between the superpowers involved:
options: A build-up of nuclear weapons and deterrence
questions.explain: Both superpowers amassed nuclear arsenals, shaping strategy through deterrence.

questions.q: Authoritarian states of the 20th century commonly maintained power through:
options: Propaganda, a secret police and one-party rule
questions.explain: Single-party regimes used persuasion and force to consolidate control.

questions.q: Comparing two authoritarian leaders' methods of gaining power uses the historical skill of:
questions.explain: Comparing and contrasting cases is a core IB History analytical skill.

questions.q: 'Change and continuity' as a concept examines:
options: What changed and what stayed the same over time
questions.explain: Change and continuity assesses developments and persistence across a period.

questions.q: Considering 'perspectives' in history means:
options: Taking account of different viewpoints and interpretations
questions.explain: Perspectives recognises that people and historians interpret events differently.

questions.q: Debating whether ideology or security fears better explain the origins of the Cold War is an example of:
questions.explain: Weighing rival explanations is central to analysing causation in history.

questions.q: The concept of 'significance' asks historians to consider:
options: Why an event or development mattered and its impact
questions.explain: Significance evaluates importance and lasting impact.

specSource: IB Diploma History guide (first assessment 2020); World history topics (Paper 2), including the Cold War
